To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total-variation norm is suitable for extracting the structural information from images and that the choice of the textural norm depends on the texture type.
the L2 model is the most appropriate for smooth images, G for piecewise smooth images, L1 for piecewise constant images, and TV-G for textures with high frequency components, such as natural images.

the total-variation functional should be used for the structural part, that for the textural component, the L2 norm should be used for smooth textures, the L1 norm is the most suitable for piece-wise smooth textures, the G norm is the best for textures with a high frequency spectrum, and the Gabor norm is the most appropriate for textures with a low frequency spectrum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modeling, algorithms and parameter selection for image splitting into structural and textural components, which is a basic and important step in image processing.
the following questions: What is the best energy term for the textural component?
the development of a general theory and algorithms that can be used for a variety of image decomposition problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the G model is the best for natural images and that the TV-G model is the best when the textural part is sparse.
the Gabor-based norm, which is the most complicated one, is also the most suitable for texture images.

the L1 model is the most suitable for textures with sharp discontinuities, the G model is the best for smooth textures, and the TV-L2 model is the best when the textural part is a mixture between smooth and sharp discontinuities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how to model and solve the structure-texture decomposition problem for various types of textures and have provided efficient tools for selecting the splitting parameter and solving the corresponding minimization problems.
the TV-L2 model is best suited for natural images, while the TV-L1 model is best suited to extract the structural part in textured images.
the L2 and G models are suitable for textures that are well represented by a single scale, while the L1 and Gabor models are suitable for multiscale textures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful selection of the splitting parameter and of the functional space for ρ may result in a significant gain in the quality of the decomposition.
the decomposition of an image into its structural and textural components is a very useful and flexible tool for many applications.
the decomposition is not a one-model-fits-all problem, and we provide a set of tools that help to decide which model to use.
